findings.title: Alternative-heading analysis can respawn across invocations
findings.claim: The current skill checks Taskfleet’s permitted alternative analysis heading only after spawning, allowing repeat workers on later invocations.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the alternate-heading check before classification and spawning.
findings.evidence: The current Step 2 reuses both exact and parsed alternative analysis before classifying an unclear bug; the section-scoped regression assertion pins that ordering.

findings.title: Settlement failure states are under-specified
findings.claim: The current skill can lose run correlation or diagnostics and lacks bounded recovery for partial, timed-out, malformed, or unreadable worker states.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain slug/run pairs and define bounded wait plus per-run fallback handling.
findings.evidence: Step 3 now retains `(slug, run id)` pairs, checks supervisors, uses a two-hour wait, handles every wait exit class, and treats malformed reports or shows as incomplete.

findings.title: Landing semantics treat every false value as unknown
findings.claim: The current skill treats every `landed: false` as uncertain instead of distinguishing `unverified` from git-verified non-landing.
findings.evidence: The current text explicitly says unverified is unknown and git-verified `landed: false` is confirmed non-landing, matching Taskfleet 0.7.1.

findings.title: Close layout still implies legacy paths
findings.claim: The current skill says closing status changes move issues into legacy `issues/closed/` storage.
findings.suggested_fix: Document flat unarchived paths, separate archive movement, and explain the legacy-named output flag.
findings.evidence: The current skill documents flat unarchived paths and bucketed archives, and explains that `moved_to_closed` signals a lifecycle transition rather than a flat-directory move.

findings.title: Issuectl should recognize both analysis headings
findings.claim: Issuectl should broaden its exact analysis projection to recognize Taskfleet’s alternative heading in this patch.
findings.suggested_fix: Teach issuectl to project both headings.
findings.evidence: The task is a shipped caller-contract alignment, and the current exact-heading projection remains intentional. The localized parsed-H2 caller compatibility path resolves this patch without redefining CLI output.

findings.title: Issuectl intake JSON paths are unwrapped
findings.claim: The skill’s `.data.body` and `.data.analysis` paths do not exist because intake handlers print unwrapped JSON.
findings.suggested_fix: Use top-level JSON paths or wrap the handlers.
findings.evidence: Worktree-local `issuectl intake queue --json` empirically emits the standard schema envelope. The handler data is wrapped by the shared command output layer.

findings.title: Generated skill copies are absent
findings.claim: The templates changed without regenerating all Claude, pi, and Codex copies.
findings.evidence: Every affected generated copy is present in the branch diff, and both `dogfooded_copies_match_templates` and the focused wellformedness test pass.

findings.title: Branch reverts broken-pipe work
findings.claim: This branch authors a rollback of the broken-pipe fix and its tests, issue state, changelog, and review history.
findings.evidence: The claim came from a two-dot diff after main advanced. `git diff main...HEAD` contains no broken-pipe paths; rebasing onto current main preserves that independently landed work.

findings.title: Taskfleet version-specific prose creates maintenance pressure
findings.claim: Hard-coded Taskfleet 0.7.1 compatibility prose can become stale after a future Taskfleet release.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace version-specific prose with a capability contract.
findings.evidence: The version-specific text is deliberate evidence for this released-contract fix. Drift occurs only after a future Taskfleet contract change, and replacing it now would not simplify the current exact compatibility explanation.
